scope: Operator-licensed local worker. READY is a statement about the development workstation where the evidence was produced; each operator must produce their own smoke proof, and the worker is unhealthy until it matches the manifest.
evidence: services/vst3-render-worker: standalone Windows worker hosting the operator's VST3 instrument in-process with pedalboard 0.9.24 (GPL-3.0, separate process behind HTTP).

Smoke on Steinberg Retrologue 2.4.0: real TrackModel rendered at exactly 144000 frames, -12.6 dBFS, 0 clipped frames after a reported -0.5 dB headroom gain; octave-up transposition is brighter (3720 -> 4353 Hz centroid) and removing material is quieter (-25.3 dBFS); host binary identity and digest attested. services/vst3-render-worker/release-evidence/smoke-proof.json.

API client proof: PedalboardRenderer.renderAttested() in artifacts/api-server accepted /health and /render, returned 132300 exact frames at 44.1 kHz, with trackModelSha256 and performedMaterialSha256 equal to Node-computed fixtures. services/vst3-render-worker/release-evidence/api-client-render.json.
Digest parity proven offline by tests/fixture-digests.json (Node) vs contract.py (Python), 21 unit tests.
honestLimits: Not bit-deterministic across renders (analog-modelled oscillators drift); the API contract does not require determinism and this is recorded in every proof.
Retrologue's default program ignores velocity; velocity sensitivity is recorded, not gated. Preset selection and per-track instrument routing are PR-22/PR-24.
Only Retrologue was smoke-tested. Padshop loads; HALion Sonic and Groove Agent SE were not probed past the bundle-path failure.
The studio export path additionally requires render lineage before it will call a native renderer; the end-to-end studio export through this worker is PR-22's proof, not this one's.
